title: Some Shinkansen Tickets to Increase in Price in 2027
paragraphs: Traveling on Japan's famous bullet trains, called the Shinkansen, will soon cost more on some routes.

On October 16, two railway companies, Central Japan Railway and West Japan Railway, announced that they will raise some ticket prices in 2027. The changes are for Nozomi trains, which run between Tokyo and Hakata, and Mizuho trains, which run west of Osaka.
From July 2027, the limited express fare for a trip from Tokyo to Shin-Osaka will go up by 700 yen to 15,420 yen. A trip from Tokyo to Nagoya will go up by 580 yen to 11,880 yen.
First-class seats, called Green Car seats, will also cost more. For trips starting from December 15, 2027, a Green Car ticket from Tokyo to Shin-Osaka will rise by 3,700 yen to 23,290 yen.

This is a big change for the Tokaido Shinkansen line between Tokyo and Osaka. It will be the first price increase on the line since Nozomi trains started running in 1992, not counting times when Japan's consumption tax went up.
Why are prices going up? The railway companies need more money to take care of the Shinkansen lines, which are getting old. The oldest parts were built in the 1960s.
The companies say that money from the higher Green Car prices will be used to make the trains better. For example, they plan to offer more free Wi-Fi and make the seats more comfortable.
Other railway companies in Japan have also been raising their prices recently.
